summary: A visibility expression (/VE) evaluates a group that takes no part in deciding visibility as ON, so under /Or and /Not that group decides the answer. §8.11.2.3 says a group whose intents the configuration does not cover "shall have no effect on visibility"; the /OCGs-and-/P route honours that by leaving the group out of the states it combines, but OptionalContent::operand maps state_of's None to `true`. [/Or off design] (an OFF group beside an ON group of /Intent /Design under the default /View configuration) draws the content where /OCGs [off design] /P /AnyOn hides it, and [/Not design] hides content that /OCGs [design] /P /AllOff shows. The same `true` stands for a group the properties dictionary never listed, so [/Not unlisted] hides content while /OCGs [unlisted] /P /AllOff shows it: the two routes of Table 97 disagree on the same groups. Every reader of `visibility` inherits it: BDC /OC, an XObject's and an annotation's /OC, and §8.9.5.4's alternate selection.
source: ISO 32000-2 §8.11.2.3: "If one or more of a group's intents is contained in the current configuration's set of intents, the group shall be used in determining visibility. If there is no match, the group shall have no effect on visibility." §8.11.2.2: "In evaluating a visibility expression, the ON state of an optional content group shall be equated to the boolean value true ; OFF shall be equated to false ."

summary: An imported page (§8.10.4's reference XObject with a supplied target) draws its optional content under the target's View-event states at magnification 1.0, whatever the operation and the reader's magnification are. enter_imported builds a ViewState for the target and carries the operation's purpose and magnification onto it — its comment names "§8.11.4.4's event" among the four things carried across — but the interpreter's own optional_content is replaced by a fresh OptionalContent::read(document), which applies only the View event at UNSTATED_MAGNIFICATION and no audience; the carried ViewState's reapplied states are never consulted. A target whose group is ON by /D and OFF under an /AS /Print usage application is hidden when the target itself is printed and drawn when the containing page that imports it is printed. The same holds for /Zoom (§8.11.4.4) and the reader's language and identity (Language, User), which are not carried at all.
source: ISO 32000-2 §8.11.4.5: "When a document is printed by an interactive PDF processor, usage application dictionaries with an event type Print shall be applied over the current states of optional content groups." and "Whenever there is a change to a factor that the usage application dictionaries with event type View depend on (such as zoom level), the corresponding dictionaries shall be reapplied." §8.10.4.1: the imported content replaces the proxy on the page being drawn.
